name: GLEE Persuasion
fullName: GLEE persuasion game: repeated seller signalling over privately known product quality

assignment.reference: Published GLEE persuasion family (arXiv:2410.05254) run through the official eilamshapira/GLEE implementation: seller privately observes each round's quality, sends a message, buyer decides to buy and then learns the realised quality; scored by self-gain plus the published efficiency/fairness formulas implemented in analyze/metrics.py. New design choices: one fixed configuration from the published 360-cell persuasion grid, a pinned LLM buyer opponent, an explicit quality-draw seed, and the numeric success threshold.
assignment.task: Play Alice, the seller, for 20 rounds of a GLEE persuasion game (long-living buyer, textual seller messages, complete information, p=1/3, v=2, M=10^4, price fixed). Each round, after privately observing the product's true quality, send the buyer a message; maximise the number of rounds in which the buyer buys.
assignment.observation: Per round the agent receives only its own seller-side text: the game rules and parameters, the round index, this round's true quality (high or low), and after the buyer moves, whether the buyer bought. The full seller-visible interaction history accumulates across rounds. The buyer's prompts, internal reasoning and the quality-draw seed are never shown.

actions.send_message: Emit the seller's JSON action for the current round, {"message": "<free-text recommendation to the buyer>"}, which the environment relays verbatim to the buyer before the buyer's buy/no-buy decision.

evaluation.success: Episode runs all 20 rounds and the seller's self-gain, recomputed as (number of rounds in which the buyer bought)/20 by the official PersuasionMetrics formula, is at least 0.50.
evaluation.failure: Self-gain below 0.50 after 20 rounds, or an episode aborted by repeated malformed actions (response lacking a parsable JSON object with a "message" key).
evaluation.efficiency: Among successful episodes, prefer higher self-gain; report the published outcome metrics efficiency = k_ev/n_ev and fairness = r_ev/(20-n_ev) alongside it as secondary diagnostics.

assignment.generation: Instance = the fixed JSON config (game_type "persuasion"; game_args is_myopic false, total_rounds 20, p 0.3333, v 2, c 0, product_price 10000, is_seller_know_cv true, is_buyer_know_p true, seller_message_type "text", allow_buyer_message false) launched with main.py -c, with the Python RNG used by generate_quality seeded per episode (seeds 0..N-1) so the 20 quality draws are reproducible, and a pinned buyer model id.
assignment.verification: Verify from the official run directory: game.csv (per-round nature quality rows plus both players' actions) and log_player_1.csv / log_player_2.csv (every prompt/response pair), with config.json recording parameters, date and commit. Recompute self-gain, efficiency and fairness with analyze/metrics.py PersuasionMetrics and confirm they match the logged decisions; retain logs for both successful and failed episodes.

evaluation.allocationNote: Original configuration episodes vector repeated three times; all episodes are planned, none executed as H0 runs.

otherModels.backend: local Codex CLI (lib/codex-model.mjs, prompt in driver.mjs buyerPrompt)
otherModels.sourceDeclared: claude-opus-5, temperature 0, max_tokens 512 (kept in the configuration objects)

notes: Up to 3 buyer attempts per round; a reply is accepted only if the original GLEE parser (project_buyer) accepts it.
In the train run the H0 seller answered through a plain-JSON CLI player transport (glee-plain-json-player-v1); the tool contract shown here is the driver contract.
